question: For $$A=\begin{bmatrix}2&1\\1&1\end{bmatrix}$$ and $$B=\begin{bmatrix}1&-1\\-1&2\end{bmatrix},$$ verify from the definition of inverse that $A$ is invertible and determine its inverse by examining both products $AB$ and $BA$.
explanation:
Required Condition

A square matrix $A$ is invertible if there exists a square matrix $B$ of the same order such that $AB=BA=I$.

Evaluation of $AB$

We have $$AB=\begin{bmatrix}2&1\\1&1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1&-1\\-1&2\end{bmatrix}$$ $$=\begin{bmatrix}2(1)+1(-1)&2(-1)+1(2)\\1(1)+1(-1)&1(-1)+1(2)\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{bmatrix}=I$$

Evaluation of $BA$

Similarly, $$BA=\begin{bmatrix}1&-1\\-1&2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}2&1\\1&1\end{bmatrix}$$ $$=\begin{bmatrix}1(2)+(-1)(1)&1(1)+(-1)(1)\\(-1)(2)+2(1)&(-1)(1)+2(1)\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{bmatrix}=I$$ Since $AB=BA=I$, the matrix $B$ satisfies the defining condition for the inverse of $A$. Therefore, $A$ is invertible and $$A^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}1&-1\\-1&2\end{bmatrix}$$.
